# Page 4^page=4
4Time table and classes structure 24 hours theoretical classes sensors and frontend circuits 26 hours hands-on classes (design laboratory) using STM32 microcontroller Theoretical classes can be attended in presence or through last year recordings. Recordings of the labs will be available but use them wisely! Day hour room Activity Monday 14:30 – 16:00 7.01 Lab Squad B Wednesday 8:30 – 10:00 21.0.3 Theory Friday 13:30 – 16:00 8.01 Lab Squad A

# Page 5^page=5
5Program of “Sensor Systems” (1/2) 1. Sensors and front-end circuits • Basics on sensors: definitions, classifications and characteristics. • Working principle and front-end circuits of the most employed sensors: o light and imaging (photodiode, CCD and CMOS sensor); o temperature (RTD, thermistors, thermocouple, thermal diode, IR thermometer); o magnetic field (Hall sensors, magneto-resistances); o strain and forces (strain gauges, piezoelectric sensor); o displacement, distance and proximity (capacitive, inductive, acoustic, optical, magnetic, touch sensors); o acceleration and orientation (MEMS); o audio (dynamic and condenser microphones).

# Page 6^page=6
6Program of “Sensor Systems” (2/2) 2. Microcontrollers for embedded sensors systems • Introduction on ARM-Cortex M cores, STM32F4 microcontroller by STMicroelectronics and Nucleo development board. • Basics on the main microcontrollers peripherals (GPIO, PWM, ADC, SPI, I2C, USART, etc.) and simple projects (pushbutton, blinking LED, sending strings to remote terminal, using communication interfaces, etc.). • Sensors expansion board: hardware description and details of the sensors included in the board. • Hands on activities to interface sensors (temperature, light, sound, rotation, accelerations) with the microcontroller using its peripherals and providing an output (sending data to pc or displaying on an LCD or generating a sound through a speaker). • The main developed projects will include: o readout of a temperature smart sensor with I2C interface; o measure light intensity through a Light Dependent Resistor; o detect sounds with a microphone and generate souds with a speaker; o acquisition of the x, y, z accelerations with a tri-axial accelerometer; o communicate among boards with IR communication protocols

# Page 9^page=9
9Assessment 1) Written Test (75% of the final mark) • 10 multiple choice questions (max 10 points) (sensors theory, microcontroller architecture and programming) • 2 theoretical open questions (max 10 points) • 2 laboratory open questions (max 10 points) The written test will be done in the official exam date. WeBeep “Supplementary materials”: 00 - Fac-simile - written test

# Page 10^page=10
10Assessment 2) Homework and short oral (25% of the final mark) • 10 homework: each week of the course a short Team report should be provided ✓ Homework assignments will not be graded individually. ✓ The overall assessment will consider timely submission, completeness, and effort and engagement, including the ability to identify, document, and discuss problems encountered during the work. ✓ Keep your reports concise: you are not expected to spend hours writing detailed reports. Briefly summarize what you did, what you learned, and any difficulties you encountered. • Short oral will consist in a discussion of the homework (you are expected to brig your laptop with all the projects done during the course) The short oral will be about one week after the written test, with possibility to agree for a different date with the professor. WeBeep “Supplementary materials”: 01 – Homework report template

# Page 11^page=11
11Laboratories • The labs will be organized into three parts: 1. a brief review of the homeworks, highlighting the main points for their resolution; 2. a theoretical section about microcontroller architecture, peripherals and programming 3. a subsequent practical one, focusing on a project related to the lab topic. At the end of the lab session, the teacher will provide a possible solution. • Two SS boards will be provided to each Team. Please ensure you bring your laptop and the SS board to every lab session. • Attendance is strongly recommended!

# Page 12^page=12
12Teams organization • You will choose your group members. We will provide you with an Excel file (Teams_organization) where you can create your Team. The link to the file will be added to the materials tab in Webeep and provided via e-mail, so be sure to enrol on the Webeep course as soon as possible. • If you cannot create a Team on your own, write your name in an empty/partially filled group, and we will create Teams for these remaining people. • Team members: 4-5 (preferably from different degree programs)

# Page 13^page=13
13Homework • After each lab session, a homework assignment will be given. • The due date for each lab assignment is 24 hours prior to the start of the subsequent lab session for the respective team. • Each homework task involves completing a project and preparing a report that summarizes the crucial aspects and primary challenges encountered. • The report must be uploaded in the Assignments tab in the WeBeep page of the course (one per Team). • One assignment per homework will be created. • The oral exam will be a discussion of the homework, so it is important all projects work correctly, even if you are not able to complete them for the due date. • Homework will contribute to the final mark, as explained in the Assessment modalities.
